posts.author: WaveRyder78
posts.content_md: Just wanted to get everyone's personal opinion on what color they prefer to do their holograms in. I know the norm is red, but I've seen some pretty cool green ones. The reason is, I'm looking to buy a laser. I'd like to get either a 30mW red or a 30mW green. HeNe most likely. This will drop me a couple thousand $, so I'd hate to make the wrong decision. Is there a difference making a green hologram than a red one? Any advice would be helpful. Thank you.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: It does not matter what color you start with you can make the final hologram any color you wish. I prefer gold for most holograms.

posts.author: Tony
posts.content_md:
35 mW HeNe's can be had for around $300 (bare head). You can build a supply for under $100.

I think there's more emulsions available for red...

With green, if you go to the 100mW level, the common laser is the Compass 315M which will cost you around $1500. However, with all that power, exposure times get very short and vibration is less of a problem.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **WaveRyder78:** Just wanted to get everyone's personal opinion on what color they prefer to do their holograms in. I know the norm is red, but I've seen some pretty cool green ones. The reason is, I'm looking to buy a laser. I'd like to get either a 30mW red or a 30mW green. HeNe most likely. This will drop me a couple thousand $, so I'd hate to make the wrong decision. Is there a difference making a green hologram than a red one? Any advice would be helpful. Thank you.

If you're resigned to dropping a couple of g's, keep an eye out for a Compass as Tony mentions. You can get loads of power (100mW) for $1500 and end up with very short exposure times (unless you go DCG) and extremely long coherence length.

If you only care about the final color of the hologram it won't matter what color your laser is. You can pre or post swell the emulsion to get almost any color in the rainbow.

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **WaveRyder78:** Thanks for your replies. How short exposure times are we talking about? Less than 10 sec? I think that less exposure times will be one of my keys of success. There's just so much involved with holography that my head is still spinning.

It all depends on how complex your setups are. I just finished a custom HOE with a 25mW laser and my exposures were 8 seconds. This was basically one 8" diameter collimated beam and one 2" collimated beam hitting the plate.

My average three beam transmission master (generally 5x7") exposures run anywhere from 20 to 40 seconds depending on the subject.

having 4x the power would greatly reduce that time.
